subject: ADD statement
notes: READ: ArithmeticEmitter.EmitInPlace (lines 26-44), NumericRenderer.Fold (319-332), NumericRenderer.CombineCore/CombineAdditive, ArithmeticEmitter.Snapshot (208-215), and the bind side ArithmeticBinder.BindAdd:43-47 (`BoundAddTo(addends, recv, sizeErr)`). MATCHED, first sentence: 'the initial evaluation consists of determining ... the sum of such operands' -- Fold seeds `acc = xs[0]` and folds `CombineCore(acc, "+", xs[i])` for i ascending, i.e. exactly 'in the order in which they are specified in the ADD statement'; 'the sum of the initial evaluation and the value of the data item referenced by identifier-2 is stored as the new value of identifier-2' -- `StoreArith(r.Place, num.Combine(num.FieldNum(r.Place), "+", value, ...))` reads the receiver as a sending operand and stores receiver+value back. The one-initial-evaluation shape of the incorporated Sec.14.7.7 GR4 + NOTE 3 is honoured: with more than one receiver the fold is materialised into a temp (`if (targets.Count > 1) value = Snapshot(value)`), so `ADD A TO B A C` cannot poison later receivers. Value evidence: ca6_binary_operand_composite runs `ADD BL TO F` (5 + 3 = 8 into PIC 9(11)V9(13)) and pb45_function_in_sending_operands runs `ADD FUNCTION SQRT(W-Z) TO W-R` -> `ADD-TO=0003` (1 + 2), both spec-derived goldens with the expected value written from the rule, not from an oracle. UNVERIFIED HALF -- the rule's SECOND paragraph, 'When standard-decimal arithmetic or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, the result of the initial evaluation is equivalent to (operand-11 + ... + operand-1n)': STANDARD-BINARY is rejected outright at bind (DataBinder.cs:318-320, COBOL0806, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.3 row 2 records it 'Not claimed'), so that leg has no implementation; the STANDARD-DECIMAL leg does exist -- NumericRenderer.CombineCore's `if (StandardDecimal)` branch lifts every ADD operand through `DecOperand`/CobolDec -- but NO golden exercises an ADD under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` (2014/arithmetic_standard_decimal is a COMPUTE, pb84_standard_decimal_intermediate_consumers is DIVIDE/REMAINDER). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` golden whose multi-addend ADD has an SDIDI-visible answer the native Int128 lane would give differently (e.g. an addend list whose intermediate needs more than the receiver's digits). || UPHELD. I re-read GR1 at specs/ISO_COBOL.md (14.9.2.4 rule 1) and re-derived the two halves before reading the record. Additional independent evidence FOR the first half: the code computes `identifier-2 + initial-evaluation` where GR1 prints `(initial-evaluation + identifier-2)` -- not a defect, addition is commutative in Int128, in CobolDec (decimal128 add is commutative and correctly rounded) and in IEEE binary64, so no rounding difference can arise from the swap; and NumericRenderer.Fold saves/restores the ambient `_rcv` so the initial evaluation is receiver-INDEPENDENT, matching GR4a ('the initial evaluation ... is placed in an intermediate data item'). Independent evidence FOR the unverified half: `grep -rn StandardDecimal` shows one shared CombineCore branch for every verb, so the ADD leg is code-shared but never exercised; no tests/conformance/**/*.cob names both ADD and STANDARD-DECIMAL. || REFUTED (one test-ref removed): conformance:cases/14.9.2-ADD/phrase_order_arithmetic was listed as evidence for this row and pins the ON SIZE ERROR PHRASE ORDER, not the initial evaluation or the store -- it is evidence for GR6/14.7.5, not for GR1, and stretching it here inflates the row's coverage. Dropped; the two value goldens stand. PB228 (2026-10-16), SECOND PARAGRAPH NOW PINNED: 2014/pb228_add_standard_decimal runs ADD ... TO under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL with X = 10**30, Y = -(10**30), Z = 0.0004, where an SDIDI (34 digits, 8.8.1.5.2) loses Z in X + Z, so the grouping decides the answer: ADD X Z Y TO R1 (R1 = 0) gives 0.0000 (initial evaluation (X + Z) + Y = 0; native would give 0.0004), and ADD X Y Z TO R2 (R2 = 0.0004) gives 0.0008, which only '(initial-evaluation + identifier-2)' produces - folding the receiver in first, ((R2 + X) + Y) + Z, gives 0.0004. STANDARD-BINARY is the declared non-support of Annex A.3 row 2 (COBOL0806 at bind); the rule's reachable modes are native and standard-decimal, both now value-pinned.
